Beyond 'Click Here': Crafting Accessible Link Text for Everyone

2026-10-01 3 min read

Generic link text like 'click here' or 'read more' poses significant barriers for users relying on screen readers or those with cognitive disabilities. Learn how descriptive and unique link text not only improves accessibility but also enhances overall user experience and SEO.

In the digital realm, links are the bridges connecting users to information. However, often these bridges are poorly labeled, creating frustration and confusion. Phrases like 'click here,' 'read more,' or 'learn more' might seem harmless, but for individuals using screen readers, they offer no context when navigating a page via a list of links. This lack of descriptive information directly impedes understanding and violates WCAG success criteria related to link purpose, making it difficult for users to predict where a link will take them.

The solution is simple yet powerful: make your link text descriptive and unique. Instead of 'Click Here for our latest report,' try 'Download our 2023 Accessibility Report.' Rather than 'Read More,' consider 'Learn about our WCAG audit services.' The best practice is to embed the link within relevant, descriptive text that clearly indicates the destination or function of the link. This allows users to understand the context and purpose of the link out of its surrounding content, providing a much richer and more efficient browsing experience.

Implementing accessible link text is a small change with a profound impact. It significantly improves usability for screen reader users, enhances navigation for everyone, and contributes positively to your site's search engine optimization by providing clearer signals to search engines. Moreover, it demonstrates a commitment to inclusivity, helping your business comply with accessibility standards and reach a wider audience. Start auditing your website's links today and transform your user experience from frustrating to fantastic.
